receipt.public_excerpt: the data centres needed to power the promised revolution are increasingly being financed with complex debt that investors are scouring for signs of a bubble.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports Part A. In late 2025, AI data centers were increasingly financed with debt. The same article cites Morgan Stanley's estimate that private credit could supply over half of the $1.5 trillion needed through 2028.

receipt.public_excerpt: Blue Owl, Oracle's largest data center partner, had been in talks to back the $10 billion deal but failed to reach agreement on terms

evidence_items.explanation: Supports Part B in part. Oracle's largest data center financier walked away from a $10B project in December 2025. The article says the project's lease and debt terms were less favorable. Oracle said it had other equity bidders.

receipt.public_excerpt: Investors placed orders for as many as US$126bil of Oracle bonds on Monday, edging out the prior record of US$125bil of orders when Meta Platforms Inc sold US$30bil bonds in October.

evidence_items.explanation: Contradicts Part B for the main bond market. About a month before the post, Oracle's $25B data center bond drew record orders, beating Meta's record from October 2025. The same article says the market 'comfortably absorbed' 2025's AI issuance.

receipt.public_excerpt: For weeks, Oracle Corp’s debt has been trading like junk amid concerns that its artificial intelligence (AI) investments won’t pay off for years, if at all.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports Part B for weaker borrowers. In the weeks before February 2026, the debt of a major AI data center builder was priced like junk over AI-spending worries, meaning its borrowing was getting costlier.

receipt.public_excerpt: lenders including JPMorgan and MUFG have already spent more than six months attempting to distribute roughly $38 billion in construction debt

evidence_items.explanation: Context. It implies the syndication of the $38B Oracle-linked loan had been dragging since about late 2025. It was reported after the post, so it is not decisive.

unresolved_gaps: No source from before the post directly reports that the $38B Oracle-linked loan was struggling to syndicate. That appears only in later reporting.
No aggregate measure from before the war, such as spreads or deal volumes for data-center-specific debt, was found to show a broad tightening.
